claim: We approve the hidden reference date, temporal acronym catalogue, human approval of reformulations and question versioning. The guide moves to version 1.2.
evidence: The robustness analysis showed that we need more precise rules for relative dates and acronyms.
Annotation must store an explicit reference date even when it is not shown in the visible text.
We must also distinguish official acronyms from abbreviations created by users. 'HR' may be expanded safely, but 'committee' does not identify a specific unit.
Administration uses different acronyms for the same unit across documents. We should retain a catalogue with validity periods.
For maintenance, I propose that a question not be overwritten when a rule changes. A new version will be created, while the previous version retains its validity interval.
Bilingual versions must be updated as a pair when the fact changes, even if their publication dates remain different.
